decisions.reason: As a laser workstation line that extends the firm's long-established marking know-how, it fits strongly with its absorptive capacity and can be refined through existing R&D, production and service routines rather than withdrawn.

This thermal inkjet printer remains very close to the firm's core coding applications, so the firm is well placed to learn from customer use and improve it within its established development and support system.

Because these industrial laser marking systems build directly on the firm's core competencies and are presented as a flagship direction tied to Industry 4.0 traceability, management would be very unlikely to abandon them quickly.

The compact laser marking cabin is a highly related extension of the existing laser portfolio, and the firm's in-house technical and service capabilities make continued adaptation more likely than exit despite its recent launch.

Although it serves a more specialized application, the lubricant printing system still builds on the firm's established high-resolution marking knowledge and its award recognition suggests enough market potential to justify continued support and learning.
